El PIB es el valor de todos los bienes y: GDP is the value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year. Nominal GDP uses each year's prices, $∑ p_t q_t$, and can rise just because prices rise. Real GDP uses the prices of a base year, $∑ p_0 q_t$, and only changes if more or less is produced: its change is economic growth.
El deflactor del PIB, $100 · \"PIB nomin: The GDP deflator, $100 · "nominal GDP"/"real GDP"$, measures the rise in the prices of everything that is produced. The CPI measures that of a fixed basket of what households buy (it is a Laspeyres index). Inflation is the rate of change of either.
Para comparar cantidades de años distint: To compare amounts from different years they are converted to euros of a single year by dividing by the price index: $"real" = "nominal" · "CPI"_{ref}/"CPI"_t$. A salary that rises 2 % with inflation of 3 % loses purchasing power: $(1.02/1.03) − 1 ≈ −1 %$.
Por el lado del gasto, $\"PIB\" = C + I: On the expenditure side, $"GDP" = C + I + G + X − M$. Adding net income received from abroad gives GNP; subtracting depreciation, NNP; and removing indirect taxes net of subsidies, national income, which is shared among the factors of production.
